title: Writer bets on cheaper AI agents with Palmyra X6 and a leaner harness
excerpt: Writer has launched Palmyra X6 and an upgraded harness it says can cut AI agent costs by up to 50%, betting the enterprise cost backlash has arrived.
content_html:
Writer, the enterprise AI company, has launched Palmyra X6, its new flagship model, alongside an upgraded “harness” built to do something the industry has been curiously reluctant to promise: spend fewer tokens.

The model is a post-training variation on Z.ai’s open-source GLM-5.2, and it is available to Writer’s clients from today.

The pitch arrives at a nervy moment. As agentic AI quietly multiplies the steps, and therefore the tokens, behind every task, enterprise bills have started to sting.

Writer is wagering that a cost backlash has arrived, and it is far from alone in scenting the opportunity, with Baseten raising $1.5bn on the theory that AI’s profits lie in cheap inference.

A harness, in Writer’s telling, is the orchestration layer wrapped around a model, the machinery that decides how a multi-step agent actually executes each request.

Optimise that layer, trimming the redundant calls and bloated context that agents tend to accumulate, and you cut token consumption without ever touching the model itself.

The savings, Writer says, are substantial. The company estimates that the new model and harness together cut costs by as much as 50% for basic tasks, while a Writer research paper found that harness-efficiency changes alone trimmed costs by roughly 40% on average across testing.

What makes the harness interesting is that it is model-agnostic. It works with Writer’s own models, but also with external ones served through Microsoft Azure and Amazon Bedrock, so the efficiency gains are not locked to a single vendor’s roadmap.

“The harness is the one component whose efficiency multiplies across every model an organization runs, present and future,” Writer’s researchers write, framing orchestration rather than raw model quality as the lever enterprises have been ignoring.

It is also a pointed one. Writer’s underlying claim is that the big labs have little incentive to help you spend less, because their revenue rises with every token you burn. Distrust of that arrangement is doing a lot of work in the company’s messaging.

CEO May Habib put it bluntly. “The enterprise is absolutely sick of chasing the next benchmark,” she said. “They want flattening cost.” It is a neat inversion of the usual sales script, in which each new model is faster, cleverer and, invariably, hungrier.

A wider thrift-maxxing trend, in which buyers reach for cheaper Chinese models, has already started to unsettle the valuations underpinning eventual OpenAI and Anthropic IPOs, a sign that price sensitivity is no longer a fringe concern.

Building the flagship on GLM-5.2 is telling in its own right. Rather than train a frontier model from scratch, Writer took a capable open-source base and specialised it through post-training, a route that keeps costs down and neatly matches the frugal story it is selling.

For European buyers, the framing should feel familiar. Scepticism about American hyperscalers’ incentives, and a preference for architectures that are not hostage to one provider, has been a running theme on this side of the Atlantic, and Writer is pitching straight into it.

There are caveats worth keeping in mind. Efficiency figures produced by a vendor about its own product deserve the usual pinch of salt, and “up to” 50% is not the same as a guaranteed 50%, but the direction of travel is hard to dispute.

The deeper shift is what Writer calls harness engineering: the discipline of spending fewer tokens per task rather than chasing another point on a leaderboard. If it takes hold, and the incentives increasingly suggest it will, the era of the ever-hungrier model may finally be meeting its budget.

content_html_zh:
企业人工智能公司 Writer 推出了其新旗舰机型 Palmyra X6，以及升级版“安全带”，旨在实现业界一直不愿承诺的事情：减少代币支出。

该模型是 Z.ai 开源 GLM-5.2 的训练后变体，从今天起可供 Writer 的客户使用。

球场正值紧张时刻。 随着代理人工智能悄悄地增加步骤，从而增加每项任务背后的代币，企业账单开始变得刺痛。

Writer 押注成本反弹已经到来，而且它并不是唯一一家嗅到这一机会的公司，Baseten 筹集了 15 亿美元资金，其理论是人工智能的利润在于廉价的推理。

用 Writer 的话说，线束是围绕模型的编排层，是决定多步骤代理如何实际执行每个请求的机制。

优化该层，修剪代理倾向于积累的冗余调用和臃肿的上下文，并且您可以在不触及模型本身的情况下减少令牌消耗。

作家说，节省的费用是巨大的。 该公司估计，新模型和线束一起可以将基本任务的成本削减多达 50%，而 Writer 的一篇研究论文发现，在测试中，仅线束效率的改变就可以平均削减约 40% 的成本。

该线束的有趣之处在于它与模型无关。 它可以与 Writer 自己的模型配合使用，也可以与通过 Microsoft Azure 和 Amazon Bedrock 提供服务的外部模型配合使用，因此效率提升不会局限于单个供应商的路线图。

Writer 的研究人员写道：“该工具是一个组件，其效率在组织当前和未来运行的每个模型中都会成倍增加。”他们将编排而不是原始模型质量作为企业一直忽视的杠杆。

也是一个尖头的。 作者的基本观点是，大型实验室没有动力帮助你减少支出，因为他们的收入随着你燃烧的每一个代币而增加。 对这种安排的不信任在公司的信息传递中发挥了很大作用。

首席执行官 May Habib 直言不讳。 “企业绝对厌倦了追逐下一个基准，”她说。 “他们希望降低成本。” 这是对通常销售脚本的巧妙逆转，其中每个新模型都更快、更聪明，而且总是更饥饿。

更广泛的节俭最大化趋势，即买家寻求更便宜的中国型号，已经开始动摇支撑最终 OpenAI 和 Anthropic IPO 的估值，这表明价格敏感性不再是一个边缘问题。

在 GLM-5.2 上构建旗舰产品本身就很有意义。 Writer 没有从头开始训练前沿模型，而是采用了一个强大的开源基础，并通过后期训练对其进行专业化，这是一种降低成本并与其所推销的节俭故事完美匹配的路线。

对于欧洲买家来说，这种框架应该很熟悉。 对美国超大规模企业激励措施的怀疑，以及对不受制于某一提供商的架构的偏好，一直是大西洋彼岸的一个持续主题，作家正在直接探讨这一主题。

有一些注意事项值得牢记。 供应商提供的关于其自有产品的效率数据值得我们通常持怀疑态度，“高达”50% 与保证的 50% 并不相同，但发展方向是无可争议的。

更深层次的转变是作家所说的利用工程：在每个任务上花费更少的代币而不是追逐排行榜上的另一个点的纪律。 如果它能站稳脚跟，而且越来越多的激励措施表明它会站稳脚跟，那么饥饿模式的时代可能最终会达到预算。
